name: webdatatools-dev-mcp
description: Developer, app & research data tools for AI agents over MCP, backed by WebDataTools' Apify Actors. Uses your own Apify API token — billed to you, not us.
long_description:
36 developer, app & research data tools. npm/PyPI/Crates package health, GitHub repo health and trending, VS Code and Chrome Web Store extensions, Google Play and App Store apps, CrossRef DOIs, openFDA recalls, iCal feeds, Shopify products, Hacker News and Stack Exchange.

Every tool call runs a WebDataTools Actor on your own Apify account (get a free token with monthly free credit at https://console.apify.com/settings/integrations), so usage is billed to you, never to the server author. The price per result is in each tool description.

apify_token.title: Apify API token
apify_token.description: Your personal Apify API token. Get a free one (with monthly free credit) at https://console.apify.com/settings/integrations. Every tool call is billed to this account, never to the server author.

tools.name: package_health_checker
tools.description: Package health checker for npm, PyPI and Crates.io — deprecation, last publish date, licence, weekly downloads, maintainers, GitHub stars and a 0-100 health score, one row per package. Billed to your own Apify account: ~$0.002 per result (Apify free-plan price, lower on paid plans).

packages.description: Packages — Enter the packages to check, one row is returned per package. Prefix the name with the registry, e.g. npm:react, pypi:requests, crates:serde. Bare names such as react or @scope/name use the default registry below, and full registry URLs work too, e.g. https://pypi.org/project/requests/. Example: ["react"].

defaultRegistry.description: Default registry — Select which registry a bare package name belongs to, e.g. npm for react. Entries that already carry a prefix (pypi:requests) or a registry URL ignore this setting. Options: npm = npm (JavaScript); pypi = PyPI (Python); crates = Crates.io (Rust).

enrichGithub.description: Enrich with GitHub data — Keep this on to add GitHub stars, forks, open issues, the archived flag and the last push date whenever the package points at a GitHub repository. Turn it off to run faster and avoid GitHub rate limits.

tools.name: github_repo_health
tools.description: GitHub Repository Health & Activity Report returns stars, commit activity, contributors, latest release and community-health files for any repo list or org:<name> — one scored row per repo. Billed to your own Apify account: ~$0.002 per result (Apify free-plan price, lower on paid plans).

repos.description: Repositories or organisations — Enter GitHub repositories to check, one row is returned per repository, e.g. apify/crawlee. Full GitHub URLs also work (https://github.com/expressjs/express), and org:<name> (e.g. org:apify) expands to that organisation's public repositories, up to Org repo limit. Example: ["apify/crawlee"].

includeContributors.description: Include contributor count — Keep this on to fetch an estimated contributor count for each repository (one extra API request per repo). Turn it off to save requests when you only need stars, activity and release data.

includeReleases.description: Include latest release — Keep this on to fetch the 5 most recent releases per repository (one extra API request per repo) and report the latest one. Turn it off for repositories that don't use GitHub Releases to save requests.

orgRepoLimit.description: Org repo limit — Enter the maximum number of repositories to pull from each org:<name> entry, e.g. 30. Repositories are sorted by most recently updated first, so a low limit still gets the organisation's most active projects.

tools.name: vscode_marketplace_extensions
tools.description: VS Code Marketplace Extension Scraper returns installs, ratings, version, categories, tags, repository and license for any VS Code extension id, marketplace URL or search keyword — one row per extension. Billed to your own Apify account: ~$0.0015 per result (Apify free-plan price, lower on paid plans).

queries.description: Extensions or searches — Enter what to look up, one row is returned per matched extension. Three formats work: an extension id like ms-python.python, a full marketplace URL like https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=esbenp.prettier-vscode, or search:<keyword> (e.g. search:prettier) to return the top matching extensions for that keyword. Example: ["ms-python.python"].

searchLimit.description: Search result limit — Enter the maximum number of extensions to return per search:<keyword> entry, e.g. 25. Extension id and URL lookups always return exactly one row and ignore this setting.

tools.name: chrome_web_store_extensions
tools.description: Chrome Web Store Extension Scraper returns users, rating, version, size, category and developer contact for any Chrome extension id or store URL — one row per extension. Billed to your own Apify account: ~$0.0015 per result (Apify free-plan price, lower on paid plans).

extensions.description: Extensions — Enter Chrome extensions to look up, one row is returned per extension. Accepts a 32-character extension id such as kbfnbcaeplbcioakkpcpgfkobkghlhen (uBlock Origin), or a full Chrome Web Store URL such as https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/grammarly/kbfnbcaeplbcioakkpcpgfkobkghlhen — the slug in the URL is ignored, only the id matters. Example: ["kbfnbcaeplbcioakkpcpgfkobkghlhen"].

tools.name: google_play_scraper
tools.description: Google Play Scraper returns app title, developer, rating, price, installs, category, media links, and optional reviews for any package id, Play Store URL or search term — one row per app. Billed to your own Apify account: ~$0.002 per app (Apify free-plan price, lower on paid plans).

apps.description: Apps — Enter the apps to scrape, one row is returned per app. Use the package id, e.g. com.spotify.music, a full Play Store URL, e.g. https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.spotify.music, or search:<term>, e.g. search:meditation, to scrape the top search results for a term. Example: ["com.spotify.music"].

country.description: Country — Enter the 2-letter country code for the Play Store storefront to read, e.g. us, gb, de. Pricing, availability and installs shown can differ by country.

language.description: Language — Enter the 2-letter language code for the app title, description and other text, e.g. en, es, de.

searchLimit.description: Search result limit — Enter how many apps to return per search:<term> entry, e.g. 20. A single Play Store search page load returns roughly 20-30 unauthenticated results with no further pagination, so this is a ceiling, not a guarantee.

includeReviews.description: Include reviews — Turn this on to add the newest reviews for each app (capped by "Max reviews per app"). Uses the same unauthenticated batchexecute endpoint the open-source google-play-scraper npm package uses for reviews — no login required, but it is an undocumented Google endpoint and could change without notice.

maxReviewsPerApp.description: Max reviews per app — Enter how many of the newest reviews to fetch per app when "Include reviews" is on, e.g. 50. Ignored when "Include reviews" is off.

tools.name: app_store_lookup
tools.description: App Store lookup for iOS apps: ratings, price, version, update date, size, genres and description from any app id, bundle id, store URL or search term — plus Top Free and Top Paid charts. Billed to your own Apify account: ~$0.001 per result (Apify free-plan price, lower on paid plans).

mode.description: Mode — Choose lookup to resolve the apps you list below, or topCharts to download a storefront's Top Free or Top Paid chart. In topCharts mode the apps field is ignored and chart, chartLimit and country decide the output. Options: lookup = Lookup apps I list; topCharts = Top charts for a country.

apps.description: Apps to look up — Enter one app per row in any of four forms: a numeric App Store id (324684580), a bundle id (com.spotify.client), an App Store URL (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/spotify-music/id324684580), or a search term prefixed with search: (search:meditation, which returns up to searchLimit apps). Used in lookup mode only. Example: ["324684580"].

country.description: Storefront country — Enter the two-letter country code of the App Store storefront to read, e.g. us, gb, de, jp. Prices, ratings, descriptions and chart positions are all storefront-specific, so us and de can return different numbers for the same app.

searchLimit.description: Results per search term — Enter how many apps each search: term should return, e.g. 25. Apple's Search API caps this at 200. Only affects rows starting with search: — an id or bundle id always returns exactly one row.

chart.description: Chart — Pick which chart to download in topCharts mode. Apple's public RSS feed serves only these two for apps — there is no top-grossing feed (it returns HTTP 404). Options: top-free = Top Free Apps; top-paid = Top Paid Apps.

chartLimit.description: Chart size — Enter how many ranked apps to return in topCharts mode, e.g. 50. Apple's feed only serves 10, 25, 50 or 100 positions; any other number (including this field's own min/max) is rounded up to the nearest one of those four.

enrichChartApps.description: Enrich chart rows with full metadata — Keep this on so every charted app also gets its ratings, price, version, size and description from the iTunes lookup API. Apple's chart feed alone only carries name, developer, icon and release date. Turning it off makes a 100-app chart two requests cheaper but leaves those columns null.

tools.name: crossref_doi_lookup
tools.description: CrossRef DOI & Citation Metadata Lookup resolves DOIs, DOI URLs or citations via the CrossRef API and returns title, authors, journal, citation count, abstract and license — one row per item. Billed to your own Apify account: ~$0.001 per result (Apify free-plan price, lower on paid plans).

items.description: DOIs, DOI URLs or citations — Enter one item per line: a bare DOI (10.1038/nature12373), a DOI URL (https://doi.org/10.1145/3292500.3330919), or free text to search — prefix free text with "search:" (search:Attention is all you need) or just paste a title/citation and it is searched automatically when it does not look like a DOI. Example: ["10.1038/nature12373"].

mailto.description: Contact e-mail (polite pool) — Optional. Enter your e-mail, e.g. you@example.com, to be added to the User-Agent and as a mailto= query param so CrossRef routes your requests to its faster "polite pool". Leave empty to use the public pool.

searchRows.description: Search results per query — Enter how many candidate works CrossRef should return for each free-text search item, e.g. 3. Only the best match (highest score) becomes the row; a higher number only improves matching, it does not create extra rows. Max 20.

tools.name: openfda_recall_monitor
tools.description: FDA Recalls & Adverse Events Monitor returns food, drug and device recalls, drug and device adverse-event reports, and drug labels from openFDA — one flat, scored row per record for a date range you choose. Billed to your own Apify account: ~$0.002 per result (Apify free-plan price, lower on paid plans).

dataset.description: Dataset — Choose which openFDA dataset to query. Enforcement datasets are product recalls; event datasets are adverse-event reports; drug-label returns FDA drug label (SPL) documents. Options: food-enforcement = Food recalls (enforcement); drug-enforcement = Drug recalls (enforcement); device-enforcement = Device recalls (enforcement); drug-event = Drug adverse events (FAERS); device-event = Device adverse events (MAUDE); drug-label = Drug labels (SPL). Example: "food-enforcement".

searchQuery.description: openFDA search query — Optional. A raw openFDA search expression, ANDed with the date range, e.g. recalling_firm:"Nestle" or classification:"Class I". Leave blank to fetch every record in the date range. See https://open.fda.gov/apis/query-syntax/

sinceDays.description: Since days — Enter how many days back to search, e.g. 30. Filters the dataset's report_date (enforcement) or receivedate/date_received (events) field; ignored for drug-label, which has no report date.

maxItems.description: Max items — Enter the maximum number of records to return, e.g. 100. Results are fetched 100 at a time (limit=100&skip=...) until this many are collected or the dataset runs out.

tools.name: ical_calendar_extractor
tools.description: iCal / ICS Calendar Feed to Events Extractor reads any ICS or webcal:// URL and returns one row per event instance, expanding RRULE recurring events within a date window, with times converted to UTC. Billed to your own Apify account: ~$0.0005 per result (Apify free-plan price, lower on paid plans).

feeds.description: ICS feed URLs — Enter the ICS/iCal feed URLs to read, e.g. https://www.officeholidays.com/ics/usa. A webcal:// URL is accepted too and automatically rewritten to https://. One row is returned per event instance found in the feed. Example: ["https://www.officeholidays.com/ics/usa"].

from.description: From date — Only return event instances starting on or after this ISO date, e.g. 2026-01-01. Leave blank to default to 30 days before today. Example: "2026-01-01".

to.description: To date — Only return event instances starting on or before this ISO date, e.g. 2026-12-31. Leave blank to default to 365 days after today. Example: "2026-12-31".

expandRecurring.description: Expand recurring events — Keep this on to expand RRULE recurring events (e.g. a weekly meeting) into one row per occurrence inside the from/to window, capped at 500 instances per event. Turn it off to get a single row per recurring event at its original start time.

maxEventsPerFeed.description: Max event rows per feed — Enter the maximum number of event-instance rows to keep per feed, e.g. 1000. The earliest instances within the window are kept first when a feed has more than this.

tools.name: shopify_products_scraper
tools.description: Shopify products scraper for catalog and variant exports: prices, discounts, SKUs, availability and images. Export CSV or JSON from public store feeds, with one row per product or variant. Review run summaries for failures and budget-limited exports. No Shopify API key required. Billed to your own Apify account: ~$0.001 per result (Apify free-plan price, lower on paid plans).

stores.description: Store URLs — Enter the Shopify store URLs to scrape, e.g. https://www.allbirds.com. A bare domain such as allbirds.com also works. Every store is checked against its public products.json feed; non-Shopify or password-protected stores get one error row instead of crashing the run. Example: ["https://www.allbirds.com"].

maxProductsPerStore.description: Max products per store — Enter the maximum number of products to fetch per store, e.g. 250. Products are paged 250 at a time from products.json, so 250 is a single page; raise it for a full catalog export, up to 20000.

collectionHandles.description: Collection handles (optional) — Optionally enter collection handles to scrape instead of the whole catalog, e.g. mens-shoes. Each handle is fetched from /collections/<handle>/products.json. Leave empty to scrape every product in the store via /products.json.

includeVariants.description: One row per variant — Keep this on to get one dataset row per product variant (size/color), with its own price, SKU and stock. Turn it off to get one row per product with aggregated minPrice, maxPrice and anyAvailable instead.

onlyAvailable.description: Only available (in-stock) items — Keep this off to include out-of-stock variants and products. Turn it on to drop any variant (or, in product mode, any product) that is not currently available for sale.

tools.name: hacker_news_scraper
tools.description: Search Hacker News stories, comments, Show HN and Ask HN posts by keyword, or pull the current front page — via the free Algolia HN API, no API key. One row per story or comment with points, author, comment count and text. Billed to your own Apify account: ~$0.0005 per Story (Apify free-plan price, lower on paid plans).

queries.description: Search queries — Enter one search term per row, e.g. apify or rust. Leave a row empty, or type front_page, to fetch the current Hacker News front page instead of running a search. Example: ["front_page"].

contentType.description: Content type — Choose which kind of Hacker News item to search: story (links and text posts), comment, show_hn, ask_hn, poll, or all to search every type. Ignored for front_page queries, which always return front-page stories. Options: story = Stories; comment = Comments; show_hn = Show HN; ask_hn = Ask HN; poll = Polls; all = All types.

sortBy.description: Sort by — relevance uses Algolia's default ranking (Hacker News' own /search), date returns the newest items first (/search_by_date), and points sorts the matched items by score, highest first. Ignored for front_page queries. Options: relevance = Relevance; date = Newest first; points = Highest points first.

minPoints.description: Minimum points — Enter the minimum score an item must have to be included, e.g. 50. Set to 0 to disable this filter.

maxResults.description: Max results per query — Enter how many rows to return for each entry in queries, e.g. 50. Algolia serves at most 1000 hits per query.

author.description: Author username — Enter a Hacker News username, e.g. pg, to only return items posted by that user. Leave empty to include every author.

sinceDays.description: Only items from the last N days — Enter how many days back to search, e.g. 7 for the last week. Set to 0 to disable this filter and search all time.

tools.name: github_trending_scraper
tools.description: Scrapes github.com/trending: the daily, weekly or monthly trending repositories or developers, by programming language and spoken language. One row per repo or developer with stars, forks, stars-in-period and description — no API key, no proxies. Billed to your own Apify account: ~$0.002 per Repository (Apify free-plan price, lower on paid plans).

languages.description: Programming languages — Enter one GitHub language slug per row, e.g. javascript or python. Leave a row empty to fetch trending across all languages. Example: [""].

since.description: Time range — Choose the trending window: daily, weekly or monthly, matching the tabs on github.com/trending. Options: daily = Daily; weekly = Weekly; monthly = Monthly.

spokenLanguage.description: Spoken language — Enter a two-letter spoken-language code to filter by, e.g. en or ja, matching GitHub's "Spoken Language" trending filter. Leave empty for all spoken languages.

mode.description: Mode — Choose repositories for github.com/trending (one row per trending repo), or developers for github.com/trending/developers (one row per trending developer). Options: repositories = Trending repositories; developers = Trending developers.

maxResults.description: Max results per language — Enter how many rows to return for each entry in languages, e.g. 25. GitHub's trending page lists at most 25 repositories or 25 developers per language.

tools.name: stackexchange_scraper
tools.description: Search Stack Overflow or any Stack Exchange site's free public API by keyword or tag and get one row per question — score, tags, author, view/answer counts and the accepted answer's text. Billed to your own Apify account: ~$0.0005 per Question (Apify free-plan price, lower on paid plans).

queries.description: Search queries — Enter one search phrase per row, e.g. web scraping, playwright timeout. Each query is run separately against the chosen site and returns its own set of question rows. Example: ["web scraping"].

site.description: Site — Enter the Stack Exchange site's API parameter, e.g. stackoverflow, superuser, serverfault, askubuntu, math.stackexchange, or any other site slug from https://stackexchange.com/sites.

tagged.description: Tags (optional) — Enter tags to narrow every query to, e.g. python, playwright. Leave empty to search all tags. Combined with each entry in Search queries.

sortBy.description: Sort by — Choose how results are ordered before Max results per query is applied. relevance ranks by text match to the query, votes by score, creation by newest first, and activity by most recently active. Options: relevance = Relevance; votes = Votes (score); creation = Creation date; activity = Last activity.

minScore.description: Minimum score — Enter the minimum question score (upvotes minus downvotes) to keep, e.g. 0. Questions scoring lower are dropped after fetching.

includeAnswers.description: Include accepted answer — Turn this on to add the accepted answer's full text as acceptedAnswerBody. Leave off for faster, smaller runs — most questions do not have one, and this field stays null when they don't.

maxResults.description: Max results per query — Enter the maximum number of questions to return per query, e.g. 50.

tools.name: bulk_image_downloader
tools.description: Download images from URLs and store them in the key-value store with metadata including dimensions, file size, and SHA256 hash. Supports bulk input from URLs or from another Actor's dataset. Billed to your own Apify account: ~$0.001 per image (Apify free-plan price, lower on paid plans).

imageUrls.description: Image URLs — Direct image URLs to download, one per line, e.g. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:FilePath/Cat03.jpg. Pages that are not images are skipped (not charged). Example: ["https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:FilePath/Cat03.jpg"].

datasetId.description: Dataset ID (optional) — Alternatively, read image URLs from another Actor's dataset. Leave empty to use imageUrls instead. Example: "".

urlField.description: URL field name — When using datasetId, the name of the field containing the image URL(s). Default: url.

maxImages.description: Max images — Maximum number of images to download. Default: 50.

maxFileSizeMb.description: Max file size (MB) — Skip images larger than this size. Default: 20 MB.

timeoutSecs.description: Request timeout (seconds) — Timeout for image downloads. Default: 30 seconds.

createZip.description: Create ZIP file — Also store all downloaded images as a single ZIP file. Default: false.

tools.name: google_flights_scraper
tools.description: Scrape Google Flights for any route and date: price, airlines, flight numbers, departure and arrival times, duration, stops and layovers, aircraft, legroom and CO2. One-way or round trip, any cabin. No login. Billed to your own Apify account: ~$0.002 per flight (Apify free-plan price, lower on paid plans).

from.description: From — Origin airports or cities, several separated by `;` (e.g. `JFK; EWR` or `New York`). Example: "JFK".

to.description: To — Destination airports or cities, several separated by `;`. Every origin is searched to every destination. Example: "LHR; CDG".

departureDates.description: Departure dates — One or more dates `YYYY-MM-DD`, separated by `;` (e.g. `2026-11-12; 2026-11-19`). Defaults to 30 days from today. Example: "2026-11-12".

returnDate.description: Return date — Optional `YYYY-MM-DD` for a round trip. Prices are then for the whole trip.

tripLengthDays.description: Trip length (days) — Optional: a round trip returning this many days after each departure date (instead of one fixed return date).

cabinClass.description: Cabin — Cabin class. Options: economy = Economy; premium_economy = Premium economy; business = Business; first = First.

adults.description: Adults — Passengers; the price is the total for all of them.

currency.description: Currency — ISO currency code for prices (USD, EUR, GBP, TRY…).

maxFlightsPerSearch.description: Max flights per search — For each route × date (Google shows up to about 100).

tools.name: google_hotels_scraper
tools.description: Scrape Google Hotels for any city and dates: nightly and total price, hotel class, rating, review count, coordinates, website, check-in times, description, nearby places and photo. No login. Billed to your own Apify account: ~$0.002 per hotel (Apify free-plan price, lower on paid plans).

locations.description: Locations — Cities, areas or neighbourhoods, several separated by `;` (e.g. `Paris; London Soho; Istanbul Sultanahmet`). Example: "Paris; London".

checkIn.description: Check-in — `YYYY-MM-DD`. Defaults to 30 days from today. Example: "2026-11-12".

checkOut.description: Check-out — `YYYY-MM-DD`. Defaults to two nights after check-in (one night if only check-in is given). Example: "2026-11-15".

currency.description: Currency — ISO currency code for prices (USD, EUR, GBP…).

maxHotels.description: Max hotels per location — Google’s results page lists about 18–20 hotels.

tools.name: booking_scraper
tools.description: Scrape Booking.com hotel search results for any destination and dates: property name, area, distance, review score and count, stars, price with taxes, discount, room type, free cancellation, breakfast and deals. Real browser, no login. Billed to your own Apify account: ~$0.001 per property (Apify free-plan price, lower on paid plans).

destinations.description: Destinations — City, region, district or hotel name, several separated by `;` (e.g. `Lisbon; Paris; Shibuya, Tokyo`). Example: "Lisbon".

searchUrls.description: Booking.com search URLs — Optional: search result URLs copied from booking.com with your filters (price, stars, property type, review score). Dates and guests in the URL are kept.

checkIn.description: Check-in — Real calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Empty: 30 days from today. Impossible dates (such as February 30) fail before browser startup.

checkOut.description: Check-out — Real calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Empty: 2 nights after check-in. Impossible supplied dates are rejected.

currency.description: Currency — ISO code for prices, e.g. `USD`, `EUR`, `GBP`, `TRY`.

sortBy.description: Sort by — Booking.com order of the results. Options: popularity = Our top picks; price = Price (lowest first); review_score = Review score; distance = Distance from centre; stars = Property rating.

maxHotels.description: Max properties per search — For each destination or URL. Booking.com lists up to about 1,000 per search.

maxSearchTimeSecs.description: Time limit per search (seconds) — Bounds requests and retries per keyword/destination. Default 90 seconds. Browser startup and final storage cleanup may add overhead. Valid partial results remain available; source failures are listed in Quality report.

tools.name: airbnb_scraper
tools.description: Scrape Airbnb search results for any destination and dates: stay name, type, area, coordinates, rating and review count, Superhost and Guest favorite badges, total and per-night price, discounts, bedrooms, beds, baths, free cancellation, photos. Billed to your own Apify account: ~$0.001 per stay (Apify free-plan price, lower on paid plans).

locations.description: Locations — City, region or neighbourhood, several separated by `;` (e.g. `Lisbon, Portugal; Bali; Brooklyn, NY`). Example: "Lisbon, Portugal".

searchUrls.description: Airbnb search URLs — Optional: search URLs copied from airbnb.com (`airbnb.com/s/...`) with your filters (amenities, map area, property type). Dates and guests in the URL are kept.

checkIn.description: Check-in — YYYY-MM-DD. Empty: 30 days from today.

checkOut.description: Check-out — YYYY-MM-DD. Empty: 2 nights after check-in.

roomType.description: Type of place — Entire homes, private rooms, shared rooms or hotel rooms only. Options: any = Any type; entire = Entire home; private = Private room; shared = Shared room; hotel = Hotel room.

minPrice.description: Min price per night — In the chosen currency.

maxPrice.description: Max price per night — In the chosen currency.

currency.description: Currency — ISO code for prices, e.g. `USD`, `EUR`, `GBP`, `TRY`.

maxListings.description: Max stays per search — For each location or URL. Airbnb shows up to about 270 stays (15 pages) per search.

tools.name: aliexpress_scraper
tools.description: Scrape AliExpress search results by keyword: product id, title, price in USD, discount, image, sponsored flag and position. Sort by price, filter by price range. No login. Billed to your own Apify account: ~$0.001 per product (Apify free-plan price, lower on paid plans).

keywords.description: Search keywords — What to search AliExpress for, several keywords separated by `;` (e.g. `phone case; wireless earbuds`). Example: "wireless earbuds".

searchUrls.description: AliExpress search URLs — Optional: search URLs copied from your browser (e.g. https://www.aliexpress.com/w/wholesale-phone-case.html). The keyword is read from them.

sort.description: Sort by — Best match (AliExpress default), cheapest first, or most expensive first. Options: default = Best match; price_asc = Price: low to high; price_desc = Price: high to low.

minPrice.description: Min price (USD) — Only products from this price.

maxPrice.description: Max price (USD) — Only products up to this price.

includeAds.description: Include sponsored products — Sponsored listings appear among the results; they are flagged with `isAd`. Turn off to skip them.

maxProducts.description: Max products per keyword — Search pages hold about 60 products each.

tools.name: lazada_scraper
tools.description: Scrape Lazada search results in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Philippines, Indonesia and Vietnam: price, original price, discount, rating, reviews, units sold, seller, brand, stock and ship-from. Billed to your own Apify account: ~$0.001 per product (Apify free-plan price, lower on paid plans).

keywords.description: Search keywords — What to search for, several separated by `;` (e.g. `phone case; power bank`). Example: "phone case".

countries.description: Countries — Lazada sites, separated by `;`: `MY` Malaysia, `SG` Singapore, `TH` Thailand, `PH` Philippines, `ID` Indonesia, `VN` Vietnam. Defaults to MY. Example: "MY; SG".

includeSponsored.description: Include sponsored products — Sponsored listings appear among the results; they are flagged with `isSponsored`. Turn off to skip them.

maxProducts.description: Max products per search — For each keyword × country (40 products per page).

maxSearchTimeSecs.description: Time limit per search (seconds) — Bounds requests and retries per keyword/destination. Default 90 seconds. Browser startup and final storage cleanup may add overhead. Valid partial results remain available; source failures are listed in Quality report.

tools.name: trendyol_scraper
tools.description: Scrape Trendyol, Turkey’s biggest online marketplace, by keyword or search URL: product name, brand, category, price, basket discount price, rating and rating count, favourites, promotions, free shipping, fast delivery and images. Billed to your own Apify account: ~$0.001 per product (Apify free-plan price, lower on paid plans).

keywords.description: Keywords — What to search on Trendyol, several separated by `;` (e.g. `kulaklık; airpods; robot süpürge`). Example: "kulaklık".

searchUrls.description: Trendyol search URLs — Optional: search URLs copied from trendyol.com (`https://www.trendyol.com/sr?q=…`) with your filters (brand, price range, seller, rating). Filters are kept.

sortBy.description: Sort by — Trendyol order of the results. Options: relevance = Recommended; price_asc = Lowest price; price_desc = Highest price; newest = Newest; best_seller = Best sellers; most_favourite = Most favourited; most_rated = Most rated.

maxProducts.description: Max products per search — For each keyword or URL (36 per page).

skipSponsored.description: Skip sponsored products — Leave out ads (they are marked `isSponsored` otherwise).

tools.name: espn_scraper
tools.description: Scrape ESPN sports data for NBA, NFL, MLB, NHL and soccer leagues: game scores and status, league standings, team lists and player rosters, from ESPN public endpoints. Billed to your own Apify account: ~$0.002 per row (Apify free-plan price, lower on paid plans).

leagues.description: Leagues — League paths as sport/league, e.g. `basketball/nba`, `football/nfl`, `baseball/mlb`, `hockey/nhl`, `soccer/eng.1` (Premier League), `soccer/esp.1` (La Liga). Example: ["basketball/nba"].

dataType.description: Data to collect — games: scores and schedule. standings: league table. teams: team list. players: team rosters. Options: games = Games and scores; standings = Standings; teams = Teams; players = Players (rosters). Example: "games".

dateFrom.description: Games from (date) — Games only. Start date as YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2026-10-22). Leave empty for today.

dateTo.description: Games to (date) — Games only. End date as YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive (max 31 days; one request per day). Leave empty to use the start date.

maxResults.description: Max results per league — Maximum rows per league. Standings and rosters are capped by what ESPN returns.

maxTeams.description: Max teams for players — Players mode only: how many teams to load rosters for.

tools.name: airbnb_reviews_scraper

listings.description: Listing URLs or IDs — One or more Airbnb listing links or numeric IDs, e.g. https://www.airbnb.com/rooms/49049534 or 49049534. Each listing returns up to "Max reviews per listing" reviews. Example: ["https://www.airbnb.com/rooms/49049534"].

maxReviews.description: Max reviews per listing — Most reviews to return for each listing, e.g. 100. Airbnb shows reviews in pages; the Actor scrolls until this number or the end of the list.

tools.name: flipkart_scraper
tools.description: Scrape Flipkart.com search results for any keyword: product title, selling price, MRP, discount, star rating, rating count (the number shown next to the stars), image and product link, in INR. keywords.description: Search keywords — Enter one or more search terms, separated by semicolons, e.g. "wireless earbuds" or "wireless earbuds; power bank". Each term returns up to "Max products per keyword" results in Flipkart search order. Example: "wireless earbuds".

maxItems.description: Max products per keyword — Most products to return for each keyword, e.g. 100. Flipkart shows 40 per page; the Actor pages through the results.

tools.name: gumtree_scraper

keywords.description: Search keywords — Enter one or more search terms, separated by semicolons, e.g. "ford fiesta" or "ford fiesta; vauxhall corsa". Each term returns up to "Max listings per keyword" results. Example: "ford fiesta".

category.description: Gumtree category — The Gumtree category slug used in the search URL, e.g. "cars", "for-sale", "property-for-sale". Leave "cars" for vehicles.

location.description: Location (optional) — Optional town or area name, e.g. "london" or "manchester". Leave empty for all of the UK.

maxItems.description: Max listings per keyword — Most listings to return for each keyword, e.g. 120. Gumtree shows 30 per page; the Actor pages through the results.

tools.name: trendyol_reviews_scraper
tools.description: Scrape Trendyol product reviews from a product URL: star rating, full text, date, seller, helpful votes, media count and the product’s rating totals. Real browser, no login. Billed to your own Apify account: ~$0.0025 per review (Apify free-plan price, lower on paid plans).

productUrls.description: Product URLs — Trendyol product page URLs, e.g. `https://www.trendyol.com/…-p-819066262`. Example: ["https://www.trendyol.com/tarcin/air-pro-2-anc-gurultu-engelleyici-bluetooth-kulaklik-ios-android-tum-telefonlar-ile-uyumlu-kulaklik-p-819066262"].

maxReviewsPerProduct.description: Max reviews per product — In Trendyol's default review order (not guaranteed newest first).

tools.name: autotrader_uk_scraper

make.description: Make — The car make as AutoTrader writes it, e.g. "Ford", "Vauxhall", "Volkswagen". Leave empty for all makes. Example: "Ford".

model.description: Model (optional) — The model within the make, e.g. "Fiesta" or "Corsa". Leave empty for all models of the make.

postcode.description: Postcode — UK postcode the distance is measured from, e.g. "SW1A 1AA" or "M1 1AE".

minPrice.description: Minimum price (GBP) — Optional lowest asking price in pounds, e.g. 1000.

maxPrice.description: Maximum price (GBP) — Optional highest asking price in pounds, e.g. 5000.

maxItems.description: Max listings — Most listings to return for this search, e.g. 100. AutoTrader shows about 25 per page; the Actor pages through.

categoryUrls.description: Best Sellers category URLs — Amazon Best Sellers pages, e.g. `https://www.amazon.com/Best-Sellers-Electronics/zgbs/electronics`. A URL keeps its own domain. Each list gives up to 100 items. Example: ["https://www.amazon.com/Best-Sellers-Electronics/zgbs/electronics"].

keywords.description: Search keywords — What to search for on coles.com.au, several separated by `;` (e.g. `milk; bread; eggs`). Example: "milk".

maxProducts.description: Max products per search — For each keyword (about 36 per page).

products.description: Products (ASIN or product URL) — ASINs (e.g. `B0BSHF7WHW`) or Amazon product URLs (e.g. `https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0BSHF7WHW`). Example: ["B0BSHF7WHW"].

searchUrls.description: Amazon search URLs — Optional: search URLs copied from Amazon (`https://www.amazon.com/s?k=…`) with your filters. Filters are kept.

maxResultsPerSearch.description: Max results per search — For each keyword or URL. Amazon shows about 16 to 24 results per page; the run follows pages until this number.

skipSponsored.description: Skip sponsored results — Leave out ads (they are marked `isSponsored` otherwise).

saveDebugHtml.description: Save debug HTML — Store the first fetched results page in the key-value store (troubleshooting only).

maxSearchTimeSecs.description: Time limit per search (seconds) — Bounds requests and retries per keyword/destination. Default 90 seconds. Browser startup and final storage cleanup may add overhead. Valid partial results remain available; source failures are listed in Quality report.

tools.name: google_patents_scraper
tools.description: Search Google Patents by keyword, assignee, inventor, country, status and date, and return one row per patent with dates, assignee, PDF link and optionally abstract, claims, CPC codes and legal status. Billed to your own Apify account: ~$0.002 per patent (Apify free-plan price, lower on paid plans).

query.description: Search keywords — Keywords to search in Google Patents, e.g. solid-state battery or "lithium iron phosphate". Leave empty when you only give patent numbers. Example: "solid-state battery".

patentNumbers.description: Patent numbers (optional) — Look up specific patents by publication number, one per line, e.g. US9123456B2 or EP3000000A1. Use this without keywords to get the full record of each patent. Example: [].

assignee.description: Assignee (company) — Only patents owned by this company or person, e.g. Tesla or Toyota. Optional.

inventor.description: Inventor name — Only patents with this inventor name, e.g. Takashi Shinmoto. Optional.

country.description: Country code — Two-letter patent office code, e.g. US, CN, EP, WO, JP, KR. Leave empty for all offices.

status.description: Status — GRANT returns granted patents only, APPLICATION returns applications only, any returns both. Options: any = Any; GRANT = Granted only; APPLICATION = Applications only.

publishedAfter.description: Published after (date) — Optional. Earliest publication date as YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. 2020-01-01.

publishedBefore.description: Published before (date) — Optional. Latest publication date as YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. 2026-12-31.

maxResults.description: Max patents — How many patents to return, e.g. 50. Google Patents returns up to 100 per page; the Actor pages until this number is reached.

includeDetails.description: Include full record — When on, each patent page is also opened for its abstract, claims, CPC codes and legal status. Slower; the price per patent is the same.
